newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.30 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.30 cent higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.30 cent a lb firmer on Monday based on market orders at 1021 EST, dealers said.
Friday, benchmark May closed down 0.90 at 73.35 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.20 to 73.10 cents. The rest of the board settled unchanged to 0.79 cent weaker.
Support in May was pegged between 73.00 and 72.50 cents and then at 70.00 cents. May's upside target was seen at 75.50.
Friday's volume was estimated at a brisk 25,000 lots.
Market analysts expect prices to consolidate at current levels where export business is expected to accelerate.

In Australia, Cyclone Justin brought heavy rains to the far northern cotton areas over the weekend, but the rains were not heavy enough to cause substantial damage to crops, Weather Services Corp, said.
It added that conditions remained favorable for planting preparations in the U.S. Delta, despite isolated showers and thunderstorms in some areas.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its first estimate of planted area for the 1997/98 crop, next Monday.
